did_you_know.text: Did you know? David and his men arrived at Ziklag on the third day and discovered that the Amalekites had raided the Negev, attacked the city, and burned it down.
Did you know? Although the Amalekites had taken captive all the women and residents, from the youngest to the oldest, the text emphasizes that they had killed no one.
Did you know? After David’s men talked about stoning him because they were bitter over the loss of their families, David found strength in the LORD his God.

Did you know? David did not immediately set out in pursuit on his own. He inquired of the LORD through the ephod whether he should pursue them, and received the answer to pursue and rescue the captives.
Did you know? David set out in pursuit with six hundred men, but when they reached the Besor Valley, some of the men stayed behind.
Did you know? Four hundred men continued with David, while two hundred stayed behind because they were too exhausted to cross the Besor Valley.

Did you know? The Egyptian man they found in the field had not eaten or drunk anything for three days and three nights. David’s men gave him bread, water, a piece of pressed fig cake, and two clusters of raisins, and his strength returned.

Did you know? The Egyptian man had been a servant of an Amalekite, but his master abandoned him after he became ill. In exchange for a promise that he would not be handed back to his master, he led David to the Amalekite camp.

Did you know? David recovered everything the Amalekites had taken, including the people, women, children, sons, and daughters, as well as the spoil. Only four hundred young men who rode camels escaped.

Did you know? David decreed that the warriors and those who stayed behind to guard the equipment would receive equal shares of the spoil. The text states that this became a statute and ordinance in Israel.
